rag_quality.judge_status: estimated (heuristic judge, no LLM API key set)
rag_quality.note: context_precision/context_recall/citation_accuracy are deterministic and always 'measured'. faithfulness/answer_relevancy depend on the judge backend -- see judge_status.

latency.scope: retrieval-only latency (dense+BM25 hybrid search against in-memory index); does NOT include LLM generation time or network latency -- run this against a live deployed API endpoint (see load_test.py) for full end-to-end request latency.

token_cost.tokenizer: word-count-approximation (tiktoken unavailable in this environment; install + allow network access to openaipublic.blob.core.windows.net for exact BPE counts)
token_cost.status: measured token counts + illustrative pricing (update PRICING dict from current provider pricing pages); monthly figures are projections based on the stated monthly_queries assumption, not observed production volume.

ingestion.scope: measures local embedding-generation throughput only (text already extracted). Does NOT include: PDF text-extraction time (PyMuPDF), network latency to an embeddings API if using a hosted model, or OCR time for scanned documents. OCR speed/accuracy requires real scanned samples and is intentionally not fabricated here -- see README.
ingestion.ocr_status: not measured -- requires a real scanned-document sample set (see README)

vector_search.scope: in-memory numpy brute-force cosine search (no ANN index, no disk I/O, no network). This is a lower bound for a real Qdrant/FAISS HNSW deployment under network+disk conditions, and an upper bound for raw compute cost at this corpus size -- report both boundaries rather than implying this equals production vector-DB latency.

cache.note: repeat_rate_assumption models a reviewer session pattern (re-querying an open document); it is an explicit simulation parameter, not an observed production traffic statistic -- re-run with your own real query logs once available.

load_test.status: not run -- requires a live deployed API endpoint. Run load_test.py separately against docker-compose or a real deployment, then merge its output CSVs here.
